summary: Uzbekistan admits citizens of the 91 countries on the Foreign Ministry's visa-free list (updated 1 June 2026) — including the whole EU, the UK, the United States, Japan, South Korea, Canada, Australia and New Zealand — visa-free, most of them for 30 days. 44 other nationalities use the USD 20 eVisa, and the rest apply at an Uzbek embassy.

currencyLimits.text: The UK Foreign Office says cash of USD 10,000 or more must be declared on entry on the written customs declaration, filled in in two copies that customs sign and stamp, that you cannot leave with more foreign currency than you brought in, and that undeclared currency may be confiscated. Canada's travel advice gives the declaration threshold as foreign currency above USD 2,000.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Uzbekistan travel advice: entry requirements

notes: The UK FCDO says importing and using drones is largely prohibited: you need a licence to import one and permission to use it before you arrive, or you can be fined or imprisoned and the equipment confiscated.

The UK FCDO says to check Uzbekistan's lists of prohibited and restricted medicines before travel, carry a doctor's prescription for prescription medicines and declare them on your customs declaration form. Some medicines sold without prescription in the UK, including codeine, cause problems on entry, and undeclared possession can lead to civil or criminal proceedings.

payments.text: The UK FCDO says internationally issued credit cards are not widely accepted outside Tashkent and the main cities, very few ATMs outside the main cities accept international cards, and you should bring enough cash or withdraw it in a main city before travelling to the regions. The Government of Canada says cards are accepted mainly in larger hotels, restaurants and cafés in major cities.

safety.text: The UK government says pickpocketing and bag-snatching are common in crowded places such as bazaars and on public transport, that terrorist attacks cannot be ruled out, and that you must carry your passport at all times because police often carry out checks.

tips.text: The UK Foreign Office says you must register within 3 days of arrival and that hotels register their guests; private hosts register you through their local OVIR or the Emehmon system. Canada's travel advice says the registration slip may be requested when you leave.
Do not bring a drone without a licence: the UK FCDO says importing or using one without permission can lead to a fine or prison sentence and confiscation.

The UK FCDO advises changing money only through official exchange booths. The Government of Canada says money can be exchanged at official counters at international airports, banks and major hotels, and that buying currency on the black market is illegal and may result in extortion or jail.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Uzbekistan?
faq.answer: Citizens of the 91 countries on the Foreign Ministry's visa-free list (updated 1 June 2026), including the whole EU, the UK, Switzerland, the United States, Japan, South Korea, Israel, Türkiye, Malaysia, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, enter visa-free, most of them for up to 30 days. 44 other nationalities, among them India, Vietnam, Thailand, Egypt and much of South America, apply for the USD 20 eVisa at e-visa.gov.uz; nationalities the portal does not list apply at an Uzbek embassy.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Uzbekistan?
faq.answer: No. The Foreign Ministry lists US citizens as visa-free for up to 30 days. For a longer stay, the Ministry says a foreign citizen must obtain one of Uzbekistan's entry visas.

faq.question: How does the Uzbekistan eVisa work?
faq.answer: Apply at e-visa.gov.uz with a passport scan and photo. The single-entry eVisa costs USD 20; the portal says applications are considered within two working days, and the eVisa allows a stay of up to 30 days and is valid for entry within 90 days. Double-entry and multiple-entry versions cost USD 35 and USD 50.

faq.question: Do I have to register my stay in Uzbekistan?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK Foreign Office says you must register within 3 days of arrival; hotels register their guests, and private hosts register you with the local OVIR or on the Emehmon electronic system. It says the authorities require a full record of where you have stayed on departure, and that missing or late registration can bring a fine for each day and possible deportation.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Uzbekistan visa-free?
faq.answer: The standard visa-free regime allows up to 30 days from crossing the border. Citizens of Azerbaijan, Georgia, Armenia, Belarus, Kazakhstan, Moldova, Russia and Ukraine have a visa-free regime of unlimited duration, and Kyrgyz citizens get 60 days. The eVisa allows stays of up to 30 days; for longer stays the Foreign Ministry says an entry visa is needed.
